biography.plain_text: Gordon White, Baron White of Hull, was a British businessman who built Hanson's American operations with his partner James Hanson. Their group became a major transatlantic conglomerate, with interests spanning coal, chemicals, building materials and consumer products. White was responsible for selecting takeover targets and directing the American business from the United States.

long_biography.plain_text:
Hanson cofounder Gordon White began his partnership with James Hanson on a much smaller scale: a greeting-card business. After selling it, they bought vehicle distributor Oswald Tillotson. Its acquisition by Wiles Group gave them substantial shares in a listed company, which they gradually brought under their control.

At Hanson Industries, White combined concentrated financial supervision with local operating freedom. Subsidiary managers could make everyday decisions within agreed limits, while the central team set budgets, measured results and controlled major spending. Acquisitions also brought cuts to head-office staffing and asset sales to repay borrowing; retained businesses received investment in expansion and modernisation.
